step1_figure.circuit_type: Closed-loop step response testbench for a two-stage class-AB op-amp without CMFB
step1_figure.description: The netlist describes the testbench from Fig 26.24, which places the basic two-stage op-amp (detailed in Fig 26.22) in a closed-loop configuration with 20k feedback resistors and 250fF load capacitors to evaluate its step response and stability.

slew_rate.description: Slew rate of the op-amp, limited by the first stage tail current charging the compensation capacitors.

equation.explanation: The maximum rate of change of the output voltage is determined by the available tail current from the diff-pair charging the Miller compensation capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the second stage (class-AB) can source/sink significantly more current than the first stage, making the first stage the bottleneck.

sky130_expected.calculation: With a typical bias current of 20 uA from the beta-multiplier and C_c = 50 fF, SR = 20 uA / 50 fF = 400 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Bias current varies with process corners and temperature, typically +/- 30%, affecting the slew rate proportionally.

quiescent_current.description: Total current drawn from the supply under DC quiescent conditions.

equation.explanation: The total current is the sum of the currents in all parallel branches of the op-amp and bias circuit.
equation.assumptions: Assumes all branches are perfectly mirrored with a 1:1 ratio from the bias circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: The op-amp has 8 branches. Assuming I_bias = 20 uA, I_DD = 8 * 20 uA = 160 uA. The bias circuit adds a few more branches, bringing the total to ~200 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the exact resistor value in the beta-multiplier and the threshold voltages of the SKY130 devices.

open_loop_dc_gain.description: Open-loop DC voltage gain of the two-stage op-amp.

equation.explanation: The total gain is the product of the first stage (cascode diff-amp) gain and the second stage (class-AB common-source) gain.
equation.assumptions: Assumes no resistive loading on the output.

sky130_expected.calculation: First stage gain ~ 40 V/V. Second stage gain ~ 12.5 V/V. Total gain ~ 500 V/V. In dB: 20 * log10(500) = 54 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Intrinsic gain (gm*ro) in SKY130 130nm is lower than older long-channel processes, so 50-60 dB is expected for a two-stage topology.

settling_time.description: Time required for the output to settle within a specified error band after a step input.

equation.explanation: Settling time depends on the closed-loop bandwidth and phase margin (damping factor).
equation.assumptions: Assumes linear settling (no slewing) for small steps, though large steps will include slew time.

sky130_expected.calculation: Based on the 400 V/us slew rate and high bandwidth, a 400mV step takes ~1ns to slew, plus ~1.5ns to settle linearly. Total ~2.5 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Load capacitance (250fF) and feedback resistors (20k) create a pole that affects the damping and settling time.

common_mode_gain.description: Gain from the input common-mode voltage to the output common-mode voltage of the first stage.

equation.explanation: Measures how much the output common-mode level shifts when the input common-mode level changes.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the tail current source has finite output resistance.

sky130_expected.calculation: From the text, a 200mV change in V_CM results in a 50mV change in output. A_cm = 50/200 = 0.25 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the output resistance of the tail current source (xm15, xm16) in the SKY130 process.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure quiescent current, open-loop gain (via AC analysis of the error signal in closed-loop), slew rate, and settling time.
